repair_disposition.rationale: The failure class is still active in current authority: 39 queue rows are in estado FALLIDO, 33 of them carry a web-fetch error class, 6 of those sit at intento_count=3 and 27 fetch-class rows are below 3 with no queue write since 2026-09-01. EKB WEB-001 is active with frecuencia 46. The pipeline behaved fail-closed (no KB from missing content), so the defect is not the fail-closed stop but the missing owned, classified retry path that lets the class recur.

verification.method: Run a read-only SELECT over lf_url_queue grouped by estado, error_detail class and intento_count, and compare to lf_pipeline_runs by source_url; repeat after any change and compare with the 2026-10-29 baseline (39 FALLIDO; 33 fetch-class; intento_count 1/2/3 = 26/7/6 across all FALLIDO).
verification.expected_result: Repair still required while fetch-class FALLIDO rows with intento_count below the policy cap exist without an owned re-admission path.

material_process_graph.rationale: The failure spans a multi-stage lifecycle: queue admission, fetch, FALLIDO closure, and any re-admission. Each phase is dispositioned below; the re-admission phase is design-blocking.

symptom.statement: web.run open(url) returned Cache miss (and some 500/timeout) for queued Reevalua and Finanty URLs; the pipeline closed them FALLIDO without inventing content. 39 queue rows are FALLIDO today and EKB WEB-001 records frecuencia 46 (2026-08-24 to 2026-09-01).

immediate_cause.statement: The fetch step obtains no content for specific queued URLs, so the pipeline stops fail-closed at capture and writes FALLIDO with a WEB_FETCH_* error_detail.

systemic_root_cause.statement: FALLIDO is a single end state shared by different failure classes (33 fetch-class, 5 ANALYSIS_LIFECYCLE_INCOMPLETE, 1 HITL) and no owned, evidenced consumer re-admits fetch-class rows by a classified retry rule; the transient external failure therefore accumulates and recurs instead of being retried or retired. The registered root cause (external fetch/cache unavailable) explains the trigger, not the recurrence.
missing_evidence: Retry rule text OP-4 from the ACT-0058 SKILL source (EV-SKILL) was not read.
Evidence of whether any scheduler or runner currently consumes FALLIDO rows.

causal_chain.statement: A valid URL is admitted to lf_url_queue (323 rows in total; 34 of the 39 FALLIDO rows are reevalua.com, 32 of them under /blog).

The fetch fails (WEB_FETCH_CACHE_MISS, WEB_FETCH_INTERNAL_ERROR, timeout/500) and the pipeline closes the row FALLIDO with error_detail and increments intento_count, creating no capture, decision or KB.
No owned consumer applies a classified retry rule to FALLIDO rows: 33 fetch-class rows stay below or at the cap with no queue write since 2026-09-01, and the same class returns in later batches.
missing_evidence: Live consumer or scheduler of FALLIDO re-admission not evidenced.

first_bad_control.statement: The retry/re-admission control for FALLIDO rows (ACT-0058 retry rule) has no evidenced enforcement point or owner, and its counter is split: intento_count lives on lf_url_queue while the declared retry gate is bound to the pipeline run.
missing_evidence: Owner of ACT-0058 not recorded (owner_name null).

escape_control.statement: The EKB validation clause (each failed URL has a FAILED run, FALLIDO queue row, incremented intento_count) is a point-in-time check; no recurring reconciliation of FALLIDO rows is evidenced. Today 35 of 39 FALLIDO URLs have a FAILED pipeline run and 4 do not.
missing_evidence: Evidence of any recurring reconciliation job over FALLIDO rows.

recurrence_evidence.fact: WEB-001 active, frecuencia 46, primera_vez 2026-08-24, ultima_vez 2026-09-01, lote_origen ACT-0058-20260824.
recurrence_evidence.scope: EKB record for this failure class

recurrence_evidence.fact: error_detail classes in FALLIDO rows span 2026-07-03 to 2026-09-01 (cache miss, internal error, timeout/500, safe-open blocked) across several batches.
FALLIDO rows: reevalua.com 34, finanty.com 4, www.finanty.com 1 (39 total).

unavailable_source_assessments.rationale: The retry rule text decides the retry cap, whether the block is at >= or >, and which counter governs; these change the enforcement point and terminality of the repair. The manifest carries only its digest, and this run did not read the repository.

execution_effect_reconciliation.effect: FALLIDO queue rows stay unchanged since 2026-09-01 (33 fetch-class rows, 27 below the attempt count of 3)
execution_effect_reconciliation.declared_producer: ACT-0058 retry rule (OP-4): controlled later retry of failed URLs

authority_contradictions.declared: EKB WEB-001 validation: every failed URL has lf_pipeline_runs FAILED and lf_url_queue FALLIDO.
authority_contradictions.observed: Of 39 FALLIDO URLs, 35 have a FAILED pipeline run by source_url, 4 do not; only 20 queue rows carry pipeline_run_id and 19 of those point to a FAILED run.

should_exist_assessment.subject: FALLIDO fail-closed stop plus retry control for fetch failures in the ACT-0058 pipeline

real_consumers.consumer: Pipeline closure of failed URLs without KB creation (EKB prevention rule)

should_exist_assessment.elimination_impact: Removing the fail-closed stop would allow KB rows from non-existent content; removing the retry control leaves FALLIDO rows permanently stranded.
should_exist_assessment.native_or_existing_alternative: Reuse the existing queue columns (estado, error_detail, intento_count) and the existing ACT-0058 failed_retry rule instead of a new table or engine.

solution_depth.rationale: Authority and architecture boundaries are stable (one queue table, one orchestrator), but the retry policy and ownership are local design decisions that are still open.

research_questions: What does OP-4 say about retry cap, comparison operator and counter?
Does any runner currently re-admit FALLIDO rows?
research_assurance.external_research_rationale: Internal canonical authority decides the retry policy and ownership; external practice cannot change what the LF rule says, so no external research was run.

patterns_compared.pattern: Classified retry with attempt cap on the existing queue (reuse)
patterns_compared.fit: Uses existing columns and the ACT-0058 retry rule.
patterns_compared.tradeoff: Needs the rule text and an owner first.

patterns_compared.pattern: Leave FALLIDO terminal and rely on manual retry

alternatives.description: Keep as is: FALLIDO stays terminal and retries remain manual (NO_CHANGE).
Reuse the queue and the ACT-0058 retry rule: split FALLIDO by error class, give fetch-class rows an owned guarded re-admission under the canonical cap, and retire rows at the cap.
alternatives.blast_radius: One queue and one orchestrator operation.

alternatives.description: Create a new dedicated retry service and table outside ACT-0058.

rejected_alternatives.reason: Provisional: leaves 33 fetch-class rows stranded and does not stop recurrence of an active class (frecuencia 46).
Provisional: creates a parallel retry authority although the queue columns and the ACT-0058 retry rule already exist.

challenger_review.challenge: Is retry even desirable when the cause is an external cache that may stay unavailable?
challenger_review.resolution: Retry is bounded by a cap and the class is separated from permanent failures; rows at the cap are retired, not looped.

challenger_review.challenge: Does the attempt counter mean the same thing in the queue and in the pipeline run?
challenger_review.resolution: Not settled: intento_count (queue) and the run-level retry counter are different columns and the OP-4 text that arbitrates them was not read.

challenger_review.challenge: Could mixing ANALYSIS_LIFECYCLE_INCOMPLETE rows into the same retry path create duplicate captures?
challenger_review.resolution: Only fetch-class rows are eligible; the 5 analysis-incomplete and 1 HITL rows are excluded from the fetch retry path.

omission_discovery.finding: Reuse the existing queue table and the ACT-0058 operation; no new engine.
The fail-closed stop at fetch already works: no KB from missing content.
The retry cap and its comparison operator must come from one canonical source and one counter; the policy text is not evidenced.
No model-context transport is involved in the queue retry path.
Fetch-to-FALLIDO is observed wired; the FALLIDO-to-re-admission edge is unresolved and tracked as design-blocking in the process graph.
Not assessed beyond the stated design: no enforcement is specified yet that could break callers.
FALLIDO has no defined retire-at-cap terminal distinct from eligible-for-retry; 6 rows sit at 3 attempts and 27 fetch-class rows below 3 with no activity since 2026-09-01.
error_detail and intento_count already expose the class; a grouped readback is enough.
No credential or privilege boundary is changed; ownership of ACT-0058 is handled as an open uncertainty.
39 FALLIDO rows out of 323; volume is small and the cost impact cannot change the design.
Verification reuses the EKB validation query plus the planned regressions.

Queue lifecycle with retries is material: ownership of the retry path is unresolved (ACT-0058 owner_name null; sibling skills ACT-0054 to ACT-0057 also null) and no convention in the registry assigns it.

invariant.statement: A FALLIDO URL may be re-admitted only by the registered orchestrator, only when its error class is fetch-class and its attempt count is below the canonical cap; otherwise it stays FALLIDO and no capture, homologation, decision or KB is created.
missing_evidence: Canonical cap and operator (OP-4 not read).

hard_guard.control: Guarded re-admission check on FALLIDO rows before any new capture attempt.
hard_guard.fail_closed_condition: Block when the row is not fetch-class, when the attempt count has reached the canonical cap, or when queue state and pipeline-run state disagree.
hard_guard.observable_result: The row stays FALLIDO, intento_count is unchanged and the blocking code is written to error_detail.
missing_evidence: Exact enforcement point inside ACT-0058 is not evidenced (EV-SKILL not read).
